title: Integrated Sexual Health and Sexual Health Outreach, HIV Prevention and Support Services.
description:
Tenders are invited for the supply of Integrated Sexual Health and Sexual Health Outreach, HIV Prevention and Support Services across Greater Lincolnshire, which incorporates the administrative counties of Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire. This procurement is being undertaken by Lincolnshire County Council for and on behalf of Lincolnshire County Council, North and North East Lincolnshire Councils.\r
\r
The tender is split into three lots:\r
Lot 1 - Integrated Sexual Health Services for Lincolnshire (Lincolnshire County Council)\r
Lot 2 - Integrated Sexual Health Services for Northern Lincolnshire (North and North East Lincolnshire Councils)\r
Lot 3 - Sexual Health Outreach, HIV Prevention and Support Services across Greater Lincolnshire (Lincolnshire County Council, North and North East Lincolnshire Councils)\r
\r
A 'Greater Lincolnshire' approach is being utilised for this tender, as a joint vision between Lincolnshire County Council, North East Lincolnshire Council and North Lincolnshire Council to ensure consistency in the provision of sexual health services for the population of the Greater Lincolnshire area. This approach aims to deliver more joined up services with a single service specification and hence more consistency in service models and digital interfaces.

title: Barton-upon-Humber Principal Town Regeneration Project: Link Road
description: Barton-upon-Humber, as a Principal Town, plays an important role in facilitating North Lincolnshire Council's (NLC) and UK Government's housing and economic growth aspirations. An integrated transport network is required to unlock the growth of the town and to encourage more sustainable modes of transport. NLC have been successful in securing Levelling Up Fund (LUF) monies to deliver the "Barton Connectivity Project" which comprises the following three interventions to help grow and activate the town:  • Barton Link Road Phase 1 (01A) - This intervention will deliver Phase 1 (1.6km) of the Barton upon Humber link road. This will divert traffic from the north and east of Barton south onto the B1026 and onwards to the A15. The route of the link road has been defined following public consultation during Summer 2022. The new link road will comprise a shared footway and cycleway running alongside the carriageway, together with landscape buffering. The link road will unlock potential residential development. Once completed, the link road will help alleviate congestion by reducing the need for HGVs and through-traffic to pass through the town centre. Awarded through YORhub Framework YORcivil3.

title: Invertebrate Survey of Barton and Barrow Clay Pits, North Lincolnshire, within Humber Estuary Site of Special Scientific Interest
description:
Surveys of the invertebrates associated with key habitats (freshwater/brackish lakes, springs/seepage, marginal vegetation, reedbed and willow scrub) within the Barton and Barrow Clay Pits, North Lincolnshire, using standard sampling protocols. To characterise the invertebrate assemblages and assess their quality and condition, using Pantheon, a database tool developed by Natural England and the Centre for Ecology & Hydrology. To record brief habitat data, including salinity of the water, to aid understanding of the habitat requirements of the assemblages.To provide habitat management recommendations for the invertebrate assemblages. Surveys will focus on the best quality areas, which are within 11 SSSI units.  2 early season visits and 2 late season visits will be made between mid-April and mid-August 2023. A minimum of 8 sample locations are specified. There are sensitive areas for breeding birds, including Schedule 1 species, and instructions must be followed to avoid disturbance. Standard sampling protocols are to be used which are a combination of standardised methods, passive trapping and free-ranging searches and must include: ground searching, pond netting, spot sweeping, sweep netting, pitfall traps. There must also be a specific search for the bryozoan Lophopus crystallinus. Principal taxa to be surveyed are: Coleoptera, Diptera, Heteroptera, Homoptera, Hymenoptera, Lepidoptera, Mollusca, Neuroptera, Odonata, Trichoptera,  Spiders. Contract to start w/c 3 April 2023 and to be completed by 15 March 2024.					
					
To apply for this opportunity you must submit your quotation meeting the requirements detailed in the Request for Quotation (RFQ) attached.
Your response must be sent to morwenna.christian@naturalengland.org.uk by 17:00 on 24 March 2023.

If you have any clarification questions linked to this opportunity or the procurement process please submit these via email to morwenna.christian@naturalengland.org.uk. Please note that, unless commercially sensitive, both the question and the response will be circulated to all tenderers.

title: Smoking Cessation Mass Media Campaign - Yorkshire and Humber
description:
The Humber and North Yorkshire Centre for Excellence in Tobacco Control programme (HNY CfE), which funded by NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB, is dedicated to reducing the harm from tobacco. HNY CfE aims to reduce smoking rates, and the harm caused by tobacco amongst the local Humber and North Yorkshire population using a multi-strand approach based on best national and international evidence. The multi-strand approach includes mass media campaigns and advocacy.

NHS Humber and North Yorkshire ICB has agreed to work with local authority colleagues across, East Yorkshire, North Yorkshire, Northern Lincolnshire, West Yorkshire and South Yorkshire to pool financial resources to support the delivery of a smoking cessation mass media campaign across the Yorkshire and Humber region. This will mean the smoking cessation mass media campaign will cover the following local authority areas: Wakefield, Leeds, Kirklees, Calderdale, Bradford, Doncaster, Sheffield, Barnsley, Rotherham, in addition to Kingston upon Hull, East Riding of Yorkshire, North East Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire, City of York and North Yorkshire.

The smoking cessation mass media campaign across Yorkshire and Humber will to run over an eight-week period in Spring 2025.

description:

Bassetlaw District Council is the northernmost of Nottinghamshire's Councils and is home to over 118,000 people. It shares borders with Derbyshire, South Yorkshire and Lincolnshire and is adjacent to seven local authority areas: Bolsover, Doncaster, Mansfield, Newark & Sherwood, North Lincolnshire, Rotherham, and Central Lincolnshire, which includes West Lindsey. \r
\r
The purpose of the DWDC will be to establish a locally distinctive framework that identifies locally important design principles for the district, with a focus upon appropriate requirements and guidance to facilitate the delivery of development as identified by the Local Plan spatial strategy including Local Plan allocations. The DWDC will also need to complement and support established and emerging Neighbourhood Plans' Neighbourhood level Design Codes (NLDCs), providing the overarching design code framework for the district.\r
